content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, assignment).**

**What the document says.** The only assignment provision is § 10 (p0042): "Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld."

**Analysis.**
- *Good news:* the clause is symmetrical and uses a reasonableness standard on consent, and there is **no change-of-control language anywhere** in the agreement. Termination (§ 6, p0031–p0033) is limited to convenience-between-SOWs and uncured material breach, so RadialSpark has no exit or re-pricing right on our change of control. No walk-away trigger on that front.
- *Problem:* there is no carve-out letting Clear Capital assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets. Even the fallback position requires a successor-assignment right (on notice); here our own M&A and internal reorganizations are gated on vendor consent, which fails the fallback on a material term. There is also no bar on RadialSpark assigning to a competitor of ours.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** Minimal insertion at the end of § 10 preserving the mutual consent standard and the subcontracting restriction: Company may assign without Contractor's consent to an affiliate or a successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all assets/business, and Contractor may not assign to a Company competitor. The comment offers a mutual successor-on-notice construction as the fallback if RadialSpark pushes back.
